div.head: Mirce 2
div.ab: Ðonne bið cynges anfeald wergild six þegna wer be Myrcna laga, þæt is XXX þusend sceatta, ⁊ þæt bið ealles CXX punda.
Þonne bið cynges anfeald wergild six þegena were be Mercena lage, þæt is XXX þusend sceatta, ⁊ þæt bið ealles CXX punda.
Ðonne byð cyninges anfeald wergild syx þegena wergyld be Myrcna lage, þæt is XXX þusend sceatta, þæt bið ealles CXX punda.
Cynges anfeald wergyld biþ syx M ðegna wergylda, þæt is þryttig sceattas.
Regis simplum weregildum est sex thainorum weregildum in Mircenorum laga, hoc est XXX milia sceatta, hoc est totaliter CXX libr.
[43, 1] Sexies autem tantum erit simplum prętium regis, hoc est ducente XX librę.
Ðonne byð cyninges anfeald wergild syx þegena wergyld be Myrcna laga, þæt is XXX þusend sceatta, þæt bið ealles CXX punda.
Ferner ist des Königs einfaches Wergeld: Wer(geld hlq) von 6 Thegnas nach Mercier-Recht, das heisst 30 000 Skat, und das ist im ganzen 120 Pfund.
Further, the king's single wergild is the wer(gild, hlq) of 6 thegns by Mercian law, that is 30,000 sceattas, and that is 120 pounds in all.
Then a king's simple wergild is the wergild of six thegns by the law of the Mercians, namely 30,000 sceattas, which is 120 pounds in all.
According to the law of the Mercians, then, the king’s individual wergild is the wergild of six thanes, that is, thirty thousand sceattas, which is one hundred and twenty pounds in all.

Genau sind 120 £ = 28800 Pf. Nach Seebohm Tribal Agsax. sei der bis Offa geltende etwas leichtere Pfennig gemeint [?]. Mit XXX m̃, die Kent als Wergeld für einen Prinzen 694 zahlte, meint der Agsächs. Annalist Sceatt. (So Allen Royal prerog. 177; Kemble in Brit. rev. 1841, 70; Saxons I 153). Das m verstehen richtig als þusenda die Hss. EF. (Letzteres verderbte Hs. CD zu XXX punda [was wenig mehr als für den Thegn wäre] und B zu x̅x̅x̅ d. i. 30000 punda [unsinnig hoch]. Irrig verstand jenes m als mancus [⅛ £] Florenz [denn er rechnete es zu 3750 £ um] und 30000 auri mancis Malmesbury. Æthelweard ergänzt irrig ‘Schilling’: solidos 30000, per singulos ·16 nummis [s. Gl Schilling 8], also 2000 £: viel zu hoch. Wheloc hat gar XXX manna, was Plummer Two Sax. chron. II 34 mit Unrecht für möglich erklärt.) Schmid bezweifelt den Betrag grundlos als zu niedrig

Exactly, 120 £ = 28800 pence. According to Seebohm Tribal Agsax. the somewhat lighter penny current until Offa is meant [?]. By XXX m̃, which Kent paid in 694 as wergild for a prince, the Anglo-Saxon annalist means sceattas. (So Allen Royal prerog. 177; Kemble in Brit. rev. 1841, 70; Saxons I 153.) MSS EF correctly understand the m as þusenda. (MS CD corrupted the latter into XXX punda [which would be little more than for the thegn], and B into x̅x̅x̅, i.e. 30000 punda [absurdly high]. Florence wrongly understood that m as mancus [⅛ £] [for he converted it into 3750 £], and Malmesbury as 30000 auri mancis. Æthelweard wrongly supplies ‘shilling’: solidos 30000, per singulos ·16 nummis [see Gl Schilling 8], i.e. 2000 £: far too high. Wheloc even has XXX manna, which Plummer Two Sax. chron. II 34 wrongly declares possible.) Schmid groundlessly doubts the amount as too low

note.seg: The wergeld of six thegns by the Mercian reckoning would be 28,800 pence. What the author understood by sceat is uncertain.
